title: Ad of the Week #4: the sale ad that opens without the discount
hook: During a sale, the discount is the one thing every ad shares.
caption:
During a sale, the discount is the one thing every ad shares.
So it is the weakest thing to open with.

Ad of the Week #4 is a pattern from sale season, shown on a made-up Republic Day ad for a cookware brand. No real brand and no real results.

The structure: open on the reason to want the product, show it doing its job, then land the offer as the reason to act today.

There is a delivery reason too. In Galvor's analysis of new video ads launched May to September 2026, six or more look-alikes launched within three days each got 48% less first-month spend. Sale week is when teams launch six versions of one banner.

slides.headline: The sale ad that opens *without the discount*
slides.sub: A pattern, shown on a made-up Republic Day ad.

slides.headline: In sale week, the discount is *wallpaper*
slides.body:
Every brand in the feed has an offer.

So a percentage in the first frame tells the viewer nothing about you. It tells them there is a sale, which they knew.

The offer is a reason to act today. It is rarely the reason to want the thing.

slides.headline: Reason first, *offer last*
items: Seconds 0 to 3 — the reason to want it
Seconds 3 to 8 — the product doing its job
Seconds 8 to 12 — the offer and the end date

slides.headline: A *cookware* brand, Republic Day sale
slides.body:
Opens on a dosa lifting clean off the pan. No text.

Then the pan, the hand, the flip.

Then: 'Republic Day sale. Ends Sunday.'

The viewer wants the pan before they hear the price.

slides.headline: less first-month spend, each, for *six or more look-alikes* launched within three days
slides.sub: Sale week is when six versions of one banner go live together.
slides.source: Source: Galvor analysis · new video ads launched May–Sep 2026

slides.headline: Three checks on the *sale batch*
items: Cover the offer — does the ad still say why?
Line up the first frames — do any two match?
Count the batch — are six of them one ad?

slides.headline: Sell the reason. *Then* the price.

notes:

Hook shape: punchy plus context.
Numbers: 48% less first-month spend for six or more look-alikes launched within three days (Galvor analysis, new video ads launched May-Sep 2026, facts bank). In the caption and on the stat slide.
The example is made up and labelled as made up. No real brand is torn down.
Timing: the slot is the day after Republic Day, so it reads as a look back at sale week and a note for the next one. The seconds on slide 3 are a guide for a short ad, not a finding.
Reader: a performance marketer who has just launched a batch of Republic Day sale ads.
